tools.name: kernels
tools.description: List the kernels of your user that you can reach from this room: name, id, machine and state.

tools.name: sessions
tools.description: List the rooms (sessions) of a kernel, or with `session_id` the agents of one room. The ids you need for `request` and `events_subscribe`.

kernel.description: Kernel name or id from `kernels`; omit for this kernel.

session_id.description: A room of that kernel: list its agents instead of the rooms.

tools.name: request
tools.description: Send one kernel request for your user to another room or kernel. Without /sudo you may do there what a Room agent without /sudo may do in its own room: list and read sessions, agents and history, attach and message agents, use a room's terminals and files, and use machines. What needs /sudo in your own room needs a live /sudo window of your own turn here; owner-only requests are refused. Example: {"kernel":"my-mac","request":{"ListSessions":null}}.

kernel.description: Kernel name or id from `kernels`; omit for this kernel.

request.description: One externally tagged kernel request, for example {"ListSessions":null}. `guide` lists examples.

tools.name: events_subscribe
tools.description: Follow a room, or one agent of it, in your event inbox; `events_wait` brings what happens there.

agent_id.description: Follow only this agent of the room.

tools.name: events_wait
tools.description: Wait for pending records of the rooms and agents you follow; returns at once when some are pending and `timed_out` when none came. Keep next_cursor.

since.description: Records after this cursor; omit for all pending records.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for a record (default 60, at most 280: a provider ends a tool call that lasts longer).

tools.name: events_ack
tools.description: Acknowledge the records you handled, through a cursor `events_wait` returned.

cursor.description: Acknowledge all records through this cursor.

guide:
Chariox reach guide for Room agents. The chariox tools act in your own room; the chariox-reach tools act on other rooms and kernels of your user.
Tools:
  kernels(): List the kernels of your user that you can reach from this room: name, id, machine and state.
  sessions(kernel?, session_id?): List the rooms (sessions) of a kernel, or with `session_id` the agents of one room. The ids you need for `request` and `events_subscribe`.
  request(kernel?, request): Send one kernel request for your user to another room or kernel. Without /sudo you may do there what a Room agent without /sudo may do in its own room: list and read sessions, agents and history, attach and message agents, use a room's terminals and files, and use machines. What needs /sudo in your own room needs a live /sudo window of your own turn here; owner-only requests are refused. Example: {"kernel":"my-mac","request":{"ListSessions":null}}.
  events_subscribe(kernel, session_id, agent_id?): Follow a room, or one agent of it, in your event inbox; `events_wait` brings what happens there.
  events_wait(since?, limit?, timeout_seconds?): Wait for pending records of the rooms and agents you follow; returns at once when some are pending and `timed_out` when none came. Keep next_cursor.
  events_ack(cursor): Acknowledge the records you handled, through a cursor `events_wait` returned.
  guide(): How reach works: the tools, example requests, authority and refusal codes.
Find a kernel with kernels (its name is the machine name, or <machine>/<label>), its rooms with sessions, then send requests with request. Without a kernel argument a request runs on this kernel.
Requests for request (replace the UPPERCASE values; ids come from earlier answers):
  {"ListSessions":null}  | SessionsListed.sessions
  {"ListProjects":{"include_archived":false}}  | ProjectsListed.projects
  {"SearchWorkspaceDirectories":{"query":"NAME","limit":20}}  | WorkspaceDirectoriesSearched.directories: absolute directory paths on that machine
  {"CreateSession":{"workspace_id":"/PATH","worktree_id":"/PATH","alias":null,"slice_ref":null}}  | workspace_id and worktree_id are one such directory path; SessionCreated.session.id
  {"AttachToSession":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","client_id":"CLIENT_NAME","capability_level":"FullTerminal"}}  | SessionAttached.attachment.id; client_id is any name you pick
  {"GetSessionState":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID"}}  | SessionState: agents, prompts, output
  {"SpawnAgent":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","provider":"codex","alias":null,"model":null,"effort":null,"execution_mode":null,"permission_level":null,"worktree_id":null,"kernel_ref":null,"slice_ref":null,"worktree_placement":null,"account_profile":"PROFILE_ID"}}  | provider is claude, codex or opencode; use the chosen profile_id from ListProviderAccountProfiles, and set model and effort; AgentSpawned.agent.id
  {"SubmitPrompt":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","attachment_id":"ATTACHMENT_ID","target_agent_id":null,"prompt":"PROMPT","attachments":[]}}  | target_agent_id is an agent id, or null for the default agent
  {"CancelActivePrompt":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","attachment_id":"ATTACHMENT_ID"}}  | stops the running prompt
  {"RunShellCommand":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","attachment_id":"ATTACHMENT_ID","command":"ls","args":["-la"],"working_directory":"/PATH","timeout_ms":60000}}  | runs on that machine; ShellCommandCompleted.result has exit_code, stdout, stderr
  {"RespondToInteraction":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","interaction_id":"INTERACTION_ID","choice_id":"CHOICE_ID","custom_reply":null}}  | InteractionResponded; set custom_reply to the person's text when question.text_reply is present
A request the kernel cannot parse comes back with a message naming the expected variants and fields: read it and fix the request.
Follow rooms or single agents with events_subscribe, then events_wait and events_ack with the cursor you keep.
A record names kernel, session_id, agent_id and refs (interaction_id, run_id, task_id). A record with value.question is a decision the person may answer through you: ask the person (options are question.choices, a free reply is question.text_reply when present),
then send request RespondToInteraction with refs.interaction_id and the chosen id to the kernel the record names. Answer without asking only for an agent your user told you to drive and how to decide. You never answer a decision of your own room.
A record with a pointer and no question is the person's alone: show pointer.one_line verbatim.
Read what happened in any room of your user, without asking: request {"GetSessionHistoryOutline":{"session_id":"SESSION_ID","agent_ids":["AGENT_ID"],"latest_prompt_count":4,"include_prefetched_content":true}} (SessionHistoryOutline.agents[].turns and prefetched_blobs).
Refusals are results with a code: reach_requires_sudo (needs your user's /sudo window, as it would in your own room), excluded_for_agents and human_only (never yours), not_allowed, reach_not_available (your run cannot reach), acquisition_declined (the user declined a machine), and the kernel_* codes of an unreachable or slow kernel: retry once with the same request on kernel_request_timeout or kernel_connection_lost, read the state first on kernel_outcome_unknown.
Machines of your user's connected service: request {"ControlPlane":{"action":"capabilities"}} gives machine_allocation.revision, then {"ControlPlane":{"action":"acquire","capability_revision":"REVISION","request_id":"ANY_NEW_ID"}} (the user is usually asked to accept first; the call waits for the answer, and acquisition_declined means no).
Then {"ControlPlane":{"action":"get","allocation_ref":"REF"}} every ten seconds or so until state is ready and access_state is available; kernel_target.kernel_id is the machine's kernel for the kernel argument. stop, start and release take allocation_ref, capability_revision, a new request_id and expected_revision (the revision of the latest answer). Release the machine when you are done.
A new machine has no room. Creating one on it needs your user's /sudo window as it does in your own room: without it CreateSession answers reach_requires_sudo; ask your user to /sudo the step. Everything after (AttachToSession, RunShellCommand and the other room requests) needs no /sudo.
Human-only, never attempted by you: passkey approvals, grants, sudo approvals, secrets and credentials, relay and pairing configuration.
